events.title: Abraham journeys to the Negev and settles at Gerar
events.narrative_summary: Abraham sets out from there toward the Negev and lives between Kadesh and Shur, then sojourns in Gerar.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'From there' (20:1) follows Abraham's view of Sodom's smoke (19:27-28) from near Mamre, so it is anchored on that event's END; the text gives no gap, hence a margin of two months. Mamre to Gerar is about 64 km by road: 1.5 days by donkey at 32 km a day (urim travel); with flocks and household I take 2 days. The dwelling between Kadesh and Shur is an open-ended stay not dated by the text, so the tier is MACRO_ERA.

events.title: Abraham calls Sarah his sister and Abimelech takes her
events.narrative_summary: Abraham says of Sarah that she is his sister, and Abimelech king of Gerar sends and takes her.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: The text gives no interval after arrival (20:2). I place the taking about a month after the settling, margin one month, since the claim was made once Abraham was known in Gerar. Duration one hour is nominal. No time word, so MACRO_ERA. It falls before Isaac's birth (21:2), which the chronology keeps within the year after Gen 18.

events.title: God warns Abimelech in a night dream to return Sarah
events.narrative_summary: God comes to Abimelech in a dream and tells him he will die for taking a married woman. Abimelech, who had not touched her, pleads his innocence, and God says he restrained him, bids him return the wife of the prophet Abraham, who will pray for him, or die with all his household.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'In a dream of the night' (20:3). Abimelech had not yet approached Sarah (20:4), so the dream is the first night after the taking: anchored on the taking's END with time_of_day ASHMORET_HATICHONAH (22:00), the first such time at or after the anchor. Duration 5 hours of night, ending about 03:00, before the morning of 20:8. Tier DAY_SEQUENCE: the night is given, not an hour.

events.title: Abimelech rises early and tells his servants, who are afraid
events.narrative_summary: Abimelech rises early in the morning, calls all his servants and tells them everything; the men are very afraid.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'Rose early in the morning' (20:8): anchored on the dream's END with time_of_day BOKER (06:00), offset 0. Duration half an hour for the speech. DIURNAL_HOUR because the text gives the part of the day.

events.title: Abimelech rebukes Abraham, who explains why he said 'sister'
events.narrative_summary: Abimelech summons Abraham and asks what he has done and why. Abraham answers that he thought there was no fear of God in the place, that Sarah is also his half-sister, and that they agreed to say this wherever they went.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Continuous with the morning assembly (20:9 'then Abimelech called Abraham'): START at the END of the servants' event, no offset. The exchange takes about an hour. DAY_SEQUENCE: same day, no hour given.

events.title: Abimelech returns Sarah with livestock, servants and silver
events.narrative_summary: Abimelech gives Abraham sheep, cattle and servants, restores Sarah, offers him his land, and tells Sarah he has given her brother a thousand pieces of silver as her vindication.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Directly follows the conversation (20:14), same day; two hours to gather the gifts, margin four hours. No time word beyond the sequence: DAY_SEQUENCE.

events.title: Abraham prays and God heals Abimelech's household
events.narrative_summary: Abraham prays to God, and God heals Abimelech, his wife and his female slaves so that they bear children, for the LORD had closed every womb of his house because of Sarah.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows the restoration (20:17); God's word said Abraham would pray once she was returned (20:7). I anchor at the END of the restoration with a one-day margin because the healing may have followed hours or a day after. The closing of the wombs (20:18) is explanatory and began with the taking; the births themselves ('they bore') come later and are not dated here. DAY_SEQUENCE.

causal_edges.causal_explanation: Sarah's return is the condition God set for the prayer and the healing, which follow it (20:7, 17).
Because Abimelech takes Sarah, a married woman, God warns him in a dream that he will die (20:2-3).
God's command to return the man's wife on pain of death leads Abimelech to restore Sarah with gifts (20:7, 14).
The warning in the dream moves Abimelech to rise early and tell his servants everything (20:6-8).
God said that Abraham the prophet would pray for Abimelech and he would live; Abraham prays and God heals him (20:7, 17).

entities.etymology_meaning: Hebrew 'amah' means female servant or slave.
entities.summary_bio: The female servants of Abimelech's household. Their wombs were closed by the LORD because of Sarah, and they bear children again after Abraham's prayer.

entities.etymology_meaning: Hebrew 'avadim' means servants or royal officials.
entities.summary_bio: The court officials of the king of Gerar. Abimelech summons them at dawn and tells them about his dream, and they are greatly afraid.

entities.etymology_meaning: Unnamed; the text calls her only 'his wife'.
entities.summary_bio: The wife of the king of Gerar. She is healed with the rest of his household after Abraham prays, and is able to bear children again.

entities.etymology_meaning: Hebrew 'kesef' means silver, from a root for longing or paleness (probably).
entities.summary_bio: A thousand units of silver that Abimelech gives to Abraham, called a 'covering of the eyes' for Sarah before all who are with her. It publicly clears her name.

components.evidence_explanation: Gen 20:3 and 20:7 say he is a dead man if he does not return Sarah.
Gen 20:18 says the LORD had shut every womb in Abimelech's house because of Sarah; 20:17 shows it ended.
Gen 20:1 says he dwelt between Kadesh and Shur and sojourned in Gerar.
Gen 20:7 calls Abraham a prophet who will pray for Abimelech.
Gen 20:14 says Abimelech gave Abraham sheep, cattle, and male and female servants, and 20:16 adds a thousand pieces of silver.
Gen 20:2 says Abimelech sent and took Sarah; she is returned in 20:14.
Gen 20:8 says the men feared exceedingly on hearing the dream.

systems.name: Divine closing of wombs
systems.ancient_near_east_context: In the ancient Near East fertility was seen as a gift of the gods, so a household's barrenness was read as divine displeasure. Genesis attributes both the opening and the closing of the womb to the LORD.
rules_and_mechanics: God alone opens or shuts the womb.
The closing falls on a whole household, not only on the offender.
God alone reopens the womb; in Gen 20 he does so after the prophet's prayer (20:17).

systems.name: Divine healing
systems.ancient_near_east_context: Healing was commonly sought from gods through priests or intercessors. In Genesis, God heals directly, and a prophet's prayer is the means.
rules_and_mechanics: The healing is God's act, not the intercessor's.
God may name the intercessor whose prayer brings the healing (20:7).
Here the healing reverses God's own closing of the wombs (20:18).

systems.name: Restitution gift
systems.ancient_near_east_context: A ruler who wronged a guest or a stranger could repair it with property. Gifts served both as compensation and as a public sign that the matter was settled.
rules_and_mechanics: The wrongdoer gives goods to the wronged party.
The person wronged is returned unharmed.
A statement before witnesses clears the name of the wronged woman.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Abraham prays to God for Abimelech.
system_instances.significance_note: Abraham acts as a prophet, as God said in 20:7, and blesses the man he deceived.

system_instances.outcome_summary: God heals Abimelech, his wife and his maidservants, and they bear children.
system_instances.significance_note: The reversal closes the episode and shows the effect of the prophet's prayer.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Abimelech gives Abraham sheep, cattle, servants and a thousand pieces of silver, returns Sarah, and offers him his land.
system_instances.significance_note: The gift repairs the wrong and clears Sarah's name before her household.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Abimelech sends for Sarah and takes her.
system_instances.significance_note: The king's act triggers God's intervention to protect Sarah before she can bear Isaac.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Abraham says Sarah is his sister, and she says he is her brother (20:2, 5); Abimelech, believing them, takes her.
system_instances.significance_note: A second telling of the wife-as-sister episode (after Gen 12). It puts Sarah and the promised line at risk.

system_instances.outcome_summary: God comes to Abimelech in a night dream and warns him of death for taking another man's wife, then tells him to return her.
system_instances.significance_note: God speaks directly to a non-Israelite king and treats his integrity as a reason for mercy.

system_instances.outcome_summary: The LORD shuts every womb in Abimelech's house.
system_instances.significance_note: The plague explains why Abimelech's household is in danger and later why the healing matters.

edges.description: Abimelech gives Abraham sheep, cattle, and male and female servants.
Abimelech asks Abraham what he has done and says he brought a great sin on the kingdom.
Abimelech gives Sarah back to Abraham.
Abimelech sends for Sarah and takes her into his household.
Abimelech tells Sarah that the silver given to her brother is a covering of the eyes and clears her name.
Abraham says that Sarah his wife is his sister, and Abimelech, told so, takes her (20:2, 5).
Abraham prays to God on behalf of Abimelech and his household.
God tells Abimelech to return the man's wife, as Abraham the prophet will pray for him.
God heals Abimelech, his wife and his maidservants so that they bear children.
God says he kept Abimelech from sinning and did not let him touch Sarah.
God tells Abimelech in a dream that he will die because the woman he took is married.
